context:
You asked for the take-off to be automatic. That bends one ruling: D100 says a card that is live but no longer on hand is taken off only after your yes for that card, with no screen control.
The parts mostly exist: the hold take-off (a fresh live read, one take-off pending per card, checked after it lands). TCGplayer never goes below 0, so a doubled take-off does no harm.
This applies only to the master-set retire reason. Widening it to other reasons is a separate question.

options.gain: No extra step, and the card cannot sell after you pull it.
options.how: The pull reads TCGplayer. If more copies are live than on hand, it lowers the count at once and checks that the change landed.
options.label: Take it off at the pull
options.lose: Banchi writes to TCGplayer by itself on each live pull, and needs your seller login to be valid. A failed write leaves the pull standing and says so.

options.gain: Every TCGplayer change still rides a send you started.
options.how: The pull records the take-off as owed. The next send you start includes it.
options.label: Take it off on the next send
options.lose: The listing stays up until then, so the pulled card can sell meanwhile.

options.gain: An explicit yes per card, closest to today's rule.
options.how: The receipt offers 'Take it off TCGplayer'.
options.label: One press on the pull receipt

ref: master-set spec section 5, PR 965; D100, never delete to lower a price
title: When you pull a live card for your master set, how should TCGplayer's count come down?
why: It is what you asked for, and it closes the window in which a pulled card can sell.
